9c7e7ff0fcbca662.title: HDB Financial Services sees 34% profit jump to ₹780 crore in Q2FY27
9c7e7ff0fcbca662.summary: Non-banking financial company HDB Financial Services on Wednesday reported a 34.2 per cent surge in profit after tax to Rs 780 crore in the September quarter of FY27 driven by higher loan demand and lower provisions. The financial services entity had earned a PAT of Rs 581 crore in the year-ago period. Its net interest income rose 15.6 per cent to Rs 2,534 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, up from Rs 2,192 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, the firm said in a stock exchange filing. HDB Financial Services' total income rose 12 per cent to Rs 3,188 crore for the quarter under review from Rs 2,851 crore in the year-ago period. Loan losses and provisions declined by 2.5 per cent to Rs 730 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to Rs 748 crore recorded in the same quarter last year. The company registered a 12 per cent growth in gross loan book to Rs 1.24 lakh crore during the quarter under review compared with Rs 1.12 lakh crore

f951a3e34b05de3e.summary: The head of the International Monetary Fund said Wednesday that the US and other wealthy nations need to urgently tackle mounting global debt levels that are weighing heaviest on low-income countries and straining the global financial system. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said that while US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other US leaders recognise that the federal deficit and national debt have grown too high, just trying to grow the US economy out of its more than USD 40 trillion in national debt would not suffice. "At the fund, we believe that, growth, of course, helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments," Georgieva said at the autumn meeting of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok. "There is no magic," she said, noting some other measures would be needed. "You have to go in a direction of tightening that, bringing it down, bringing deficit down." feb149fa372c0910.title: Rupee rises 31 paise to 94.86 against US dollar during early trade
feb149fa372c0910.summary: The rupee appreciated 31 paise to 94.86 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, supported by the ongoing impact of the Reserve Bank of India's structural forex interventions and liquidity-tightening measures. Market participants attributed the rupee's continued appreciation to central bank intervention and the unwinding of long dollar positions. However, ongoing external macroeconomic pressures are likely to temper further gains, they said. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.95, then gained ground to touch 94.86, registering a gain of 31 paise over its previous close. On Wednesday, the rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar. The rupee has now crossed 95.5095.00 range, bringing 94.80 into focus, CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari said. "A sustained break below 94.80 could open the door to another 5075 paise of appreciation. And the reduced direct dollar demand from oil companies could support the momentum," Pabari .
